A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MODULI and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Their methods and experiments can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original D4MORL experiments, including benchmark scores, sliding-guidance ablations, normalization comparisons, and Pareto-front visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The written Preference Predicted Normalization objective changes from negative squared error in v1 Equation (7) to positive squared error in v2 Equation (9), consistent with the stated minimization. The planner, normalization procedures, and slider algorithms otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six D4MORL environments, Expert and Amateur data, and Complete, Shattered, and Narrow preference coverage. v2's expanded main Table 1 reproduces coverage already reported in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Complete comparisons retain MODT(P), MORvS(P), BC(P), and CQL(P); Shattered/Narrow tables retain MODT(P), MORvS(P), and BC(P). Table 7 retains CG and CFG+CG guidance comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset construction, HV/SP/RD metrics, 501/325 evaluation preferences, training budgets, and sampling settings are retained. Newly supplied baseline parameter counts and the exact next-state loss weight document existing experiments without establishing changed settings.

E4.justification: The slider ablation, normalization comparison and visualization, guidance-method comparison, and supplementary Pareto fronts are retained. New Appendix F explains the existing loss-weight trick but supplies no ablation or additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and report means and standard deviations. No new uncertainty estimation or statistical testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries in Tables 2–7 and all seven plotted figures are unchanged. v2 Table 1 reproduces the full Complete results already present in v1 Table 4, rather than adding experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Removing the erroneous negative sign from the return-prediction loss corrects its mathematical definition. The sliding-guidance derivation in Appendix D and metric definitions are retained; the added standard classifier-guidance formula is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: preference-conditioned diffusion planning, two normalization methods, sliding guidance, and improved D4MORL preference generalization. No new central scientific claim is introduced.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 moderates the interpretation of Narrow-dataset Pareto-front extension from 'significantly' to 'slightly.' The conclusion specifies low-dimensional states as the experimental limitation, replacing the broader description of structured states.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, Appendix F pseudocode specifying next-state loss weight 10, and baseline parameter counts: MORvS 8.55M, MOBC 8.83M, and MODT 9.75M. v1 already disclosed the DiT backbone and increased next-state weighting.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including CleanDiffuser, U-Net, EUCLID, and several robotics and human-feedback works. These extend contextual references without substantially revising the paper's positioning within offline MORL and diffusion planning.

P1.justification: v2 adds guided-sampling explanations, a sliding-guidance example, main-text dataset descriptions, acknowledgments, and the loss-weight appendix. Most prose and section order remain intact; former Appendices F/G become G/H.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with new running headers and extensive figure/table resizing and repositioning. Main Table 1 expands to include existing Amateur results alongside Expert results. The seven figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through the explicit loss weight, implementation pseudocode, baseline sizes, and code-access link, while correcting the return-loss sign. These are useful, limited gains: the empirical evidence is unchanged, and duplicated guidance exposition and Complete-results tables reduce concision.
